In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immune cell functions in CAPD patients and the possible correlation with the development of peritonitis and/or ultrafiltration loss.
the study of the immune response of the peritoneum in CAPD patients, and the relationship between this response and the occurrence of peritoneal infection and ultrafiltration failure.
the study of the peritoneum as an immunological organ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peritoneum of CAPD patients with a high incidence of peritonitis is characterized by an altered balance between immune activation and inhibition.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the perito neal immune response is not only important to protect the peritoneal cavity from infection, but also to prevent peritoneal sclerosis, a serious complication of CAPD, which is often the cause of ultrafiltration loss and therefore a major reason for CAPD dropout (7).
